When this is the right step

The audit says so

Your Delivery Audit shows the same pattern in more than one project: work gets stuck, scope grows unnoticed, nobody can say what comes next. A list of steps won't fix that.

You work in Notion, Excel or on a whiteboard

Then this is too big a first step. Start with the Delivery Setup. The Realign makes sense when there is a board to read.

You can stop after the first phase.

More of me at the start, less at the end. If you still need me in the last week, something went wrong.

Phase 1Two days

€7,500 fixed

On-site or remote

See how work really moves, then rebuild it

Day one

I sit in your daily meeting, open your board, and talk to the two or three people closest to planning and development. I map how work actually flows, not how it's supposed to.

Day two

We rebuild the board together, write the priority list for the next four weeks, and fix the meetings. You get my assessment in writing.

What you have on Monday

  • A board that shows what's stuck in ten seconds
  • A written priority list for four weeks
  • A daily meeting of 10 to 15 minutes
  • A clear answer to "who decides?"

You can stop here. Four weeks later we check what stuck. If it holds, we're done.

Phase 2Four to six weeks

Fixed price per team

Fewer days every week

Stay while the new setup meets real life

This is where quick fixes fail. A priority changes, a dependency doesn't land, someone shows up with something urgent. I'm there in those moments, so the team handles them with the new setup instead of the old habits.

  • Coaching in the daily meeting, at the board and in scope conversations
  • Cleaning up the backlog with your PM or tech lead
  • Adjusting the setup while we're still working together
Phase 3Two weeks

Light touch

Hand over and step back

A written handover: what changed, why, how to keep it, and what to watch. A final run of the Delivery Audit. A check-in four weeks after I leave.

Measured, not felt

Your dates are measured three times, the same way as in the Delivery Audit. You see whether the chances moved. So does your CEO.

Is this for you?

Yes, when

  • The team is capable but the setup around it isn't.
  • You tried a new board or a new meeting before, and it faded.
  • You want proof for your CEO or clients that it worked.

Look elsewhere when

Questions people ask first

Are you in our office every day?

No. The two days of phase 1, yes. In phase 2 I'm there for the moments that matter, fewer every week. Phase 3 is handover.

Can't we just run a retrospective?

You can, and you should. But a retro surfaces what the team already knows. I don't work here, so I see what nobody sees because they're too close.

What if the two days turn out to be enough?

Then that's the whole engagement. The setup is yours, and the four-week check-in tells us whether it held.

Not sure you need this?

Most people shouldn't start here. Run the Scan, or get the audit. They tell you whether the way of working is the problem.
